Live Document: A tracked Markdown file inside an active Spec folder, an open Backlog Entry, an unresolved Finding, or under `docs/references/`; a citation is a relative link destination or repository-relative path naming a file removed by retirement (ADR-0260).
Archive Relink: The Archive Command's pre-write operation that promotes a cited non-core file to `docs/references/<basename>`, rewrites Live Document citations to the promoted copy or Archive Record, and records rewritten paths under the optional `relinked` list (ADR-0260).
History Citation: A citation from tracked Markdown outside the History Root to a file or folder a selected history unit removes, which `roundfix baseline update` lists in text and JSON, binds into the Plan Digest, and may offer for `--promote` when it is a Live Document (ADR-0260).
Stale History Citation: A citation already unresolved in the working tree whose target remains in the History Full Tag, which `roundfix baseline update` reports with a `git show history-full:<path>` restore command outside the Plan Digest and update state (ADR-0260).
Archive Record: The small `<slug>.md` record an archive leaves under the resolved archive root. It carries the disposition, QA Report and verdict, promoted references, an optional `relinked` list, and `source_revision`; the removed Spec folder stays recoverable in Git at that revision. The History Sanitize Command also writes one for a Legacy Archive Folder; a folder without a QA Report receives the disposition `no-qa`, while a folder whose newest QA Report failed without an override receives `failed-qa` and keeps that verdict and report name. `failed-qa` is never a pass or an override (ADR-0248, ADR-0251, ADR-0260).
Archive Command: The support command that performs an Archive Relink, then retires a Spec under the archive eligibility contract, writes its Archive Record, and removes the Spec folder while keeping it in Git at `source_revision`. Normal QA eligibility and a user-authorized QA Archive Override are distinct dispositions. Neither retirement nor an override fabricates Task completion or a passing QA verdict (ADR-0260).
Managed Refresh: The preservation mode that regenerates only Managed Regions, leaves every other byte identical, requires no Source Baseline and no Decision Plan, and takes no root backup because the plan's preimages carry the preservation proof. It also lists History Citations, binds them into the Plan Digest, accepts repeatable `--promote` values, and converts Pending History on approval. Its preservation proof still covers the instruction carriers. It converges: a second run against an unchanged catalog reports the repository current and proposes no change (ADR-0254, ADR-0260).
